_note: Typeface reference for the Typography tab. Every family is SIL Open Font License 1.1, so self-hosting is permitted; the only obligation is to keep the licence file, which sits next to each family in assets/fonts/. Weights are the files actually present in this repo, not a wish list.

families.name: Inter
families.blurb: The default choice for product UI. Tall x-height, open apertures, a true italic, and tabular figures that actually line up in tables. Designed by Rasmus Andersson for a screen first.
families.watch: At 12px and under on a light background it can feel slightly cold. Bump letter-spacing to +0.01em rather than going heavier.

families.name: Manrope
families.blurb: A geometric sans with a slightly squared-off terminal and generous width. Reads friendly at display sizes without turning childish, which is why it keeps showing up in fintech and health branding.
families.watch: The 800 is heavy enough to be a display weight. Do not use it for body copy — the colour count is high and small sizes get congested.

families.name: Space Grotesk
families.blurb: A proportional take on Space Mono — the letterforms keep the typewriter DNA but the spacing is modern. Distinctive enough to carry a brand, neutral enough to live in a product.
families.watch: The quirky details (the angled leg on the R, the flat-topped 3) stop reading as character below about 16px.

families.name: DM Sans
families.blurb: Low-contrast and compact, optimised for small sizes. A very efficient workhorse when you need a lot of words inside a small card and the page must not feel dense.
bestFor: Landing pages with lots of copy
families.watch: Being compact, it needs slightly more line-height than Inter to stay comfortable — 1.6 rather than 1.5.

families.name: Sora
families.blurb: A geometric sans with a wide, confident rhythm and flat terminals. Built for headings, where its wide apertures hold up at large sizes without hinting artefacts.
families.watch: No 500 weight ships in this repo. If you need medium, use 600 — do not fake it with 400 and opacity, which thins the strokes unevenly.

families.name: Bricolage Grotesque
families.blurb: A variable grotesque with a real optical-size axis: the 800 is drawn for 48px+ and the 400 for small text, so one family covers display through body without looking like two.
families.watch: Because the optical axis is the point, do not set the 800 below 32px — the display cut has too much contrast for small text.

families.name: Playfair Display
families.blurb: High-contrast Didone-adjacent serif with hairline serifs and very fine joins. The most recognisable 'premium editorial' face on Google Fonts, and it earns it at display sizes.
families.watch: Hairlines vanish below 24px and the thin strokes disappear on low-DPI screens. Never use it for body copy or on a dark background without increasing the weight to at least 600.

families.name: Fraunces
families.blurb: A soft-serif with an optical 'wonk' and 'soft' axis, so you can dial the terminals from crisp to friendly without changing families. Excellent for brands that want personality but not eccentricity.
families.watch: It is a display face. At body sizes use the 400 and raise the size to at least 17px, or the wonk reads as noise.

families.name: Source Serif 4
families.blurb: Adobe's reading serif, designed for long-form legibility on screens. The most boring choice on this list and the correct one for documentation, policy pages and anything a person has to read to the end.
families.watch: It genuinely is unremarkable as a logo. That is the point — reserve it for text and let the brand live elsewhere.

families.name: Lora
families.blurb: A brushed-contrast serif with a calligraphic root. Warmer than Source Serif and less severe than Playfair, so it bridges body and display better than either.
families.watch: The 600 sits between a text and a display cut. It is the most useful weight here for subheads.

families.name: JetBrains Mono
families.blurb: A code-first monospace with a tall x-height and a slashed zero. The extra height is what makes it readable next to a UI sans at the same nominal size.
families.watch: It is wide. In a narrow table it will eat the column, so set tabular numbers only where alignment actually matters.

families.name: Space Mono
families.blurb: A quirky monospace with the proportions of an old typewriter. Only two weights ship here, which is fine — it belongs in branding and display, not in long code listings.
families.watch: Only 400 and 700. There is no medium, so do not reach for faux-medium in body text.

guides.title: Self-host, do not hotlink
guides.body: Every family here ships as woff2 in assets/fonts/<family>/<weight>.woff2. Load them from your own origin. A Google Fonts <link> means a third-party request on every page load, a privacy disclosure you now owe your users, and a layout that shifts if fonts.googleapis.com is slow or blocked.

guides.title: Subset before you ship
guides.body: These files are already latin-only, which is most of the win. If your product has a non-latin audience, add that subset explicitly rather than loading the full family — a Devanagari or Cyrillic cut is 5-10x the bytes.

guides.title: Pair one sans with one serif
guides.body: The reliable pattern is a UI sans for everything functional and a serif for long-form or brand voice. Two sans families need a strong size or weight difference to avoid looking like a mistake; two serifs almost never work without one being a clear display cut.

guides.title: Set a real type scale, not one size
guides.body: Give each step its own size, line-height and tracking. Display sizes need negative tracking because large letterforms look loose; small labels need positive tracking because they lose their shape.

guides.title: Always pair a system fallback
guides.body: font-family must end in a real fallback. If the webfont fails, the layout should still be readable on the system stack rather than falling back to the browser default serif.

guides.title: Make numbers line up
guides.body: Any figure that updates, animates or sits in a column needs tabular figures, or the digits change width and the whole layout jitters.

guides.title: Check the licence before you ship
guides.body: Every family in this tab is SIL Open Font License 1.1: use it commercially, embed it, modify it, no permission needed. Keep the LICENSE.txt that sits beside each family and do not sell the font file on its own. That is the entire obligation.
guides.code:
OFL 1.1 — what you may do:
  • use commercially, any project
  • self-host, subset, modify
  • use in a paid product

What you must do:
  • keep the licence with the font files

What you may not do:
  • sell the font by itself
  • use the reserved font names in a modified version
